title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of workers' organizations

description.narrative: The capacity of the workers organizations in Eswatini to effectively engage in dialogue for policy reform remains critical. Government has instituted a process for the review of selected labour legislation such as the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the Industrial Relations Act, the Employment Act that require an understanding and capacity for effective engagement and influence and policy engagement. Capacity needs remain for the workers organizations to engage more effectively in social dialogue. Notwithstanding strides made in the past to foster the gender responsiveness of workers organizations, much remains to be done to enhance the Workers Organizations’ capacities to mainstream gender within their organisational structures, and to promote a culture of zero tolerance towards violence and harassment within their organizational structures, and to promote a transformative agenda on gender equality, non-discrimination, and inclusion. As actors for change, the workers’ organizations in Eswatini are not optimally engaged in influencing economic, social, and environmental policies through the UN Cooperation Framework processes. The strategy will focus on capacity building support to the workers organizations on provisions of up-to-date Conventions that underpin policies and legislation under reform; leadership training and capacity support for the effective engagement of workers organizations in tripartite social dialogue; workers’ organizational capacities to mainstream gender; and facilitated engagement of workers’ organizations to influence the economic, social, and environmental policies through the processes of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework.
